clue.text: Great Persian holds priest in island

indicators.note: the Persian king's name holds the priest's letter inside it, as a container

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire

explanation.surface: A great Persian ruler keeps a priest on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean nation lying wholly on one isle, east of Crete.

clue.text: Try a hooligan — the answer's there

definitions.text: Try a hooligan — the answer's there

indicators.note: the clue tells the solver the solution is sitting in these very words, so read through them for a run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone advises trying a thug, because that is where the solution lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'trY A HOOligan', and the run is itself a word for a hooligan, so the whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's brutish humanoids gave English a word for a coarse lout or thug.

clue.text: Thrift, perhaps, works after support

indicators.note: the word for works is placed after the word for support in the answer

parts.note: a rock is something firm to lean on, a support
a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: Someone praises being careful with money once a foundation is secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrift' looks like saving money, but it is the sea pink, a small flower of cliffs and rockeries; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift, the sea pink, is an alpine-style flower grown among stones in rockeries.

clue.text: The Boy Friend, role of another youth, primarily

parts.note: to act in someone's stead is to fill the role of another person

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word youth is taken

explanation.surface: A theatre note: in The Boy Friend musical, a young actor understudies another's part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Boy Friend' is the title of a well-known British stage musical, but here it simply means a regular boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular sweetheart is called a girl's steady in informal speech.

clue.text: Drink for young Johnson?

parts.note: a baby is a young one
Samuel Johnson was nicknamed the Great Cham of literature by Smollett

explanation.surface: A question about a beverage fit for a Johnson child.
explanation.walkthrough: BABYCHAM is a sparkling perry drink long popular in Britain; 'young' modifies Johnson in the surface but supplies BABY in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A branded sparkling pear-based tipple sold in small bottles.

clue.text: Rifled mailbag returned, from which much has gone missing

definitions.text: from which much has gone missing

indicators.note: a rifled bag has been ransacked and its contents thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A postbag was sent back plundered, with much of its contents lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifled' looks like a description of the bag, but it signals that MAILBAG RETURNED is rearranged into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea area off Florida is famed in legend for ships and planes vanishing without trace.

clue.text: Search for point in G&S character -it's nonsense

indicators.note: the word for search is put in place of the word for point within the character's name

parts.note: Reginald Bunthorne is the aesthetic poet in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience
a thorn is a sharp point
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Hunting for meaning in a Gilbert and Sullivan role turns out to be rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap THORN out of BUNTHORNE and put COMB in, leaving BUN + COMB + E.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty claptrap or humbug, the word coming from a long-winded congressman for Buncombe County.

clue.text: Brake — police on one's tail

parts.note: cops is slang for the police

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, taken from one

explanation.surface: Someone braking hard with the police following close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brake' reads as slowing a car, but here it is the noun, a thicket; the tail of 'one' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is a dense thicket, the same as a small wood of undergrowth.

clue.text: Sorry rich atone — becoming this?

indicators.note: becoming tells us the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remorseful rich man makes amends by turning into a recluse.
explanation.walkthrough: RICH ATONE rearranges into the answer, and the whole clue describes a penitent wealthy person withdrawing from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious hermit who withdraws from society, as a penitent might.

clue.text: Film containing many layers

explanation.surface: A movie made up of numerous strata.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aardman animated picture about escaping poultry; also a hen enclosure, holding egg-laying birds.

clue.text: The finest tool

explanation.surface: The best of the implements.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of the bunch is its best; a pick is also a pointed digging implement.

clue.text: Show Germany going into debt for old French leader

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial show or display

indicators.note: going into means the letter for Germany is placed inside the letters for debt

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany showing off while going into debt, under a former French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb but is the noun, ceremonial display; 'going into' places Germany's letter inside the debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Pompidou was President of France from 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: Honour rule applied to King

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
on means applied to, as paint on a wall

explanation.surface: A royal honour is conferred under the rules on a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is the fairy king of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy monarch, husband of Titania.

clue.text: Hindustan native could have used it

definitions.text: Hindustan native could have used it

indicators.note: the clue says the item is to be found within its own words, which an Indian could once have handled

explanation.surface: Something an Indian person might once have spent.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'hindustAN NAtive', and the coin they spell was in use in India until 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Course with opportunity to expand trade

explanation.surface: A route offering a chance for business growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Suffolk racecourse, home of British flat racing; also a fresh outlet for selling goods.

clue.text: Food for Olympians provided by 'igh-class bank, international one

indicators.note: the dropped H in 'igh tells us to drop the H from the bank's name too

parts.note: Hambros was a well-known London merchant bank
a is one

explanation.surface: Fine food supplied by a posh bank to an overseas client.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''igh-class' copies a dropped aitch, so HAMBROS, a high-class bank, loses its H to give AMBROS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the sustenance of the gods on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Gone to Heaven for it, possibly? Not quite

definitions.text: Gone to Heaven for it, possibly? Not quite

parts.words: Gone to Heaven for it, possibly? Not quite
parts.note: someone who has not quite died but is close to death, with only part of themselves already departed

explanation.surface: Someone almost dead but not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person very old or near death.

clue.text: See 16
See tewhit flying around, right? He'd like that

indicators.note: flying around suggests the letters of tewhit scatter and rearrange

parts.note: C is the letter that sounds like see

explanation.surface: Seeing an owl's call take wing, a birdwatcher is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tewhit is the owl's call, so the clue pictures a birdwatcher thrilled by an owl; 'flying around' rearranges TEWHIT into TWIT and HE, and 'See' is heard as the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen birdwatcher would love to spot an owl.

clue.text: Sword stuck in deeper, but withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the run is read backwards
the letters are lodged inside the word deeper

explanation.surface: A blade thrust in deeper and then pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'deeper' sits EEPE; 'withdrawn' turns it back to give the fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing blade with a stiff triangular cross-section.

clue.text: It may be stormy right up in Manx town

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the town's name

parts.note: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Weather may turn stormy right over a town on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may be stormy' points to the seabird called the stormy petrel; 'up' turns the right abbreviation backwards, and 'in' sets it inside the Manx town.
explanation.definitionFit: The storm petrel is a small seabird, and a stormy one is its familiar name.

clue.text: Lackey, one paid to break record

indicators.note: the record's letters are broken open and the other pieces put in

parts.note: a log is a written record
a is one
PD is the abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: A servant is paid to smash a record.
explanation.walkthrough: A (one) and PD (paid) break into LOG (record).
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning, servile follower is called a pet dog that sits on its master.

clue.text: Dug up coarse material

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dug means mined, excavated

explanation.surface: Some rough cloth was excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Tavern a rough hole, gets custom

indicators.note: rough means roughly made, so these letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: use is custom or habit

explanation.surface: A pub that is a rough dive still gets plenty of customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'Taverna' is a misread of 'Tavern'; 'rough' signals a rearrangement of the second word only, with the 'a' kept in front unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub serving beer, an old-fashioned word for an inn.

clue.text: Writer up a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the writer's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer

explanation.surface: A writer is stuck up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or small tree, the source of a tangy spice.

clue.text: Hide knight caught in vice

indicators.note: the knight's letter is held inside the word for vice

parts.note: a sin is a vice
K is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight concealing himself, trapped in wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is the noun, an animal's pelt, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its pelt or outer covering.

clue.text: Routine procedures could produce Osram light

indicators.note: could produce means the letters may be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: An Osram bulb could give out set methods.
explanation.walkthrough: Osram is a lighting brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Step-by-step sets of rules for solving problems, as in computing.

clue.text: Team sped headlong in this

indicators.note: headlong means wildly and in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A side rushed wildly in a charging mass.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM SPED rearranges into the answer, and the whole clue pictures a herd charging.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a crowd or herd.

clue.text: Girl swallows sodium being crazy

indicators.note: the girl's name swallows the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: A girl gulps down salt and goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness or extreme foolishness is the state of the mind gone.
